purpose: Same-machine steady reach regression, measured stages at a prescribed outlet and a distinct interior sensor. Review copy only.
reach: Below RS 44506 to RS 34913, upstream of Twin Bridges. Stay within the published constant-discharge interval. Keep RS 44056 inside the reach.
geometric_source: USGS Siletz 1D distribution, archived station/elevation and georeferenced cut lines. Combined floodplain and field bathymetry, already interpreted by the study authors.
event_selection: First qualifying noon standard-time day in November-December 2017 for development, and January-February 2018 for holdout. Approved USGS 14305500 values at all 15-min steps over +/-6h, range at most 3 percent of median. Median flow 600 to 1800 cfs (development), 2200 to 3400 cfs (holdout). Both PT records must be present throughout the 12h window and above their surveyed instrument elevations. Select chronologically, without examining residuals.
availability_amendment_before_solving: No winter holdout date satisfies both the 3 percent stability criterion and the original 2200–3400 cfs interval. Based only on flow coverage and presence of sensor records, widen the upper limit to 3600 cfs. Preserve all original criteria above for audit. No modeled stage residual had been computed or inspected.
flow: Station 14305500 window median times the published RS 44506/19532 discharge ratio from the 0.995 profile (Table 14 method). Conditional ungaged transfer; timing robustness tested over the whole window.
roughness: Fix channel 0.035 and overbank 0.065 for both events before evaluating stages; within the published broad ranges and no fit to these two events.
boundary: Subcritical steady flow. Impose event-matched upstream Twin Bridges PT 986237 at the downstream XS 34913. Score only downstream Neighborhood Bar PT 9695486 at interior XS 44056. Use window medians for stability and to avoid a single time-offset dependency. Do not use computed historical profiles as observations.
tests: Report signed residual, both WSEs, period, sample ranges and count, cross-section flow and native warnings. Flag absolute differences over 0.15 m as an internal investigation threshold, not a survey accuracy or design tolerance. Rating distance scale, incomplete horizontal/time metadata, transferred discharge and spatial extrapolation remain disclosed. A failed holdout is a deliverable.
independence: Separate dates and discharges from current development and published four calibration magnitudes. Same observational campaign and previously interpreted geometry. Not independent field surveying or engineering sign-off.
